sections.content:
34,585 people

were counted on the census as "farm workers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Farm workers perform a variety of tasks, by hand and machine, to produce and harvest crops and to breed and rear cattle, sheep, pigs and poultry.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "farm workers" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "farm workers", 14.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "farm workers" was 40 to 44 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "farm workers" included:

  • fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)
  • retail cashiers and check-out operators
  • shelf fillers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "farm workers" there were more men than women (77% compared with 23%).

This means "farm workers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 77% and women made up 23% of "farm workers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "farm workers" included:

  • driving instructors
  • warehouse operatives
  • IT user support technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "farm workers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "farm workers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "farm workers", 8.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.4% compared with 22.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (76.1%) than self-employed (23.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Shropshire, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
